help.title: How to read a key signature
rules: **Sharps:** last sharp + a half step = tonic.
**Flats:** the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
**Scale notes:** start from the tonic and apply every accidental in the signature.
**Relative minor:** the 6th note of the major scale, same signature.
help.example_sharps: **3♯** → F♯, C♯, G♯ → **A major** → A, B, C♯, D, E, F♯, G♯ → relative F♯ minor.
help.example_flats: **2♭** → B♭, E♭ → **B♭ major** → B♭, C, D, E♭, F, G, A → relative G minor.
help.tip: Tip: read a flat by its “belly” — count lines and spaces up from the E on the bottom line.
help.relative_rule: **Relative minor:** the 6th note of the major scale — or go down a step and a half (3 half steps) from the tonic. Same key signature. C major → A minor; G major → E minor.
help.enharmonic_rule: **Equivalent (enharmonic):** the same sound with two names, like F♯ = G♭. Keys too: F♯ major (6♯) sounds the same as G♭ major (6♭).
help.lookup_note_single: **{note}** has no other name with a single accidental.
help.lookup_same_sound: The two keys below sound the same — only the spelling changes:

rule.why_written: The accidental written next to the note overrides the key signature.
rule.why_inherit: The accidental written earlier in the same bar still applies to this note.
rule.why_reset: The bar line cancels the accidental: the key signature applies again.
